what: Microchip Technology makes microcontrollers and related analogue, connectivity and memory chips. They sit inside cars, industrial machines, appliances and medical devices, usually in large numbers and at modest prices each.
customers: Industrial equipment makers, carmakers and their suppliers, aerospace and defence contractors, and consumer and medical device manufacturers.
money: power management, interface and timing chips
moat: Tens of thousands of customers designing its chips into products that stay in production for a decade or more, with no single customer large enough to dictate terms.
risks: Revenue fell about 18% a year over three years in a severe industrial downturn
Debt of about $5.5 billion against very little cash
Customers built up large inventories that took years to work off
Operating margin fell to about 10% from far higher levels
opportunities: Revenue grew about 7% last year as the cycle turned
Analysts see about 40% upside from current levels
Factory utilisation recovering would restore margins quickly given its high fixed costs
watch: Book-to-bill ratio and inventory levels in the channel.
